name: MIT Media Lab — AHA Program
description: Advancing Humans with AI (AHA) is a multi-faculty research program at the MIT Media Lab studying how pervasive AI shapes the human experience — and how to design human-AI interaction that fosters flourishing rather than dependence. Launched in April 2025, AHA convenes academia, industry, and civil society around moonshot research on the psychological, social, and cognitive impact of AI.

name: Human Flourishing Program · Harvard
description: Founded in 2016 at Harvard’s Institute for Quantitative Social Science, the program studies flourishing as "a state in which all aspects of a person’s life are good" — and now runs a working group applying flourishing science to AI product decisions.

name: Stanford HAI
description: The Stanford Institute for Human-Centered AI advances AI research, education, and policy to improve the human condition — with the belief that AI should be collaborative, augmentative, and enhancing to human life.

name: Wellbeing Research Centre · Oxford
description: Oxford’s centre for the science of wellbeing, studying how life circumstances — including technology — shape happiness at population scale.

name: Oxford Internet Institute
description: Oxford’s multidisciplinary department for the study of life online — home to some of the most rigorous large-scale evidence on how digital technology and games actually affect wellbeing.

name: Institute for Ethics in AI · Oxford
description: Brings philosophy to the heart of AI ethics — examining what AI means for human values, democracy, and the good life.

name: Leverhulme Centre for the Future of Intelligence
description: Cambridge’s interdisciplinary centre on the nature and impact of AI — working to ensure intelligent machines serve human values and society.

name: Center for Human-Compatible AI · Berkeley
description: UC Berkeley center reorienting AI research toward provably beneficial systems that remain uncertain about — and deferential to — human preferences.

name: Berkman Klein Center · Harvard
description: Harvard’s center for internet and society, studying AI governance, human agency, and the public interest in networked technology.

name: Princeton CITP
description: Princeton’s Center for Information Technology Policy — rigorous, skeptical scholarship on what AI can and cannot do, and what that means for society.

name: Digital Ethics Center · Yale
description: Studies the governance of digital innovation so that AI and data technologies serve human dignity and flourishing.

name: Positive Psychology Center · UPenn
description: The birthplace of positive psychology — the science of what makes life worth living — now extending flourishing research into the age of AI.

name: CMU Human-Computer Interaction Institute
description: One of the world’s leading HCI departments, designing AI systems that augment human capability, learning, and health.

name: The Alan Turing Institute
description: The UK’s national institute for data science and AI, directing research capacity toward public-good applications in health, environment, and society.

name: Contemplative Sciences Center · UVA
description: The University of Virginia’s hub for contemplative research, convening an interdisciplinary group on AI-driven interventions for wellbeing and spirituality.

name: Baylor Institute for Studies of Religion
description: Co-leads the Global Flourishing Study, bringing expertise on religion, character, and meaning to the empirical study of flourishing.

name: Anthropic · Societal Impacts
description: Anthropic’s technical research team studying how AI is actually used in the world — including large-scale analyses of values and emotional reliance in human-AI conversations, feeding directly into model safeguards.

name: OpenAI
description: Builder of ChatGPT, increasingly investing in research on the emotional and social effects of conversational AI — including a joint randomized study with the MIT Media Lab on affective use and wellbeing.

name: Google DeepMind
description: Frontier lab whose ethics research examines what advanced AI assistants owe their users — including a landmark treatise on the ethics of AI assistants and human autonomy.

name: Microsoft Research
description: Studies how generative AI reshapes cognition and work — including influential research on AI’s effect on critical thinking and "tools for thought."

name: Google Jigsaw
description: A unit within Google that builds technology to counter threats to open societies — from toxicity and harassment online to polarization — so digital spaces stay healthy for people.

name: Allen Institute for AI (Ai2)
description: A nonprofit AI lab building truly open models and applying AI to science, conservation, and the common good.

name: Center for Humane Technology
description: The advocacy nonprofit behind The Social Dilemma, working to realign technology — now AI — with humanity’s interests, warning against systems that exploit human vulnerabilities under the guise of assistance.

name: All Tech Is Human
description: Builds and unites the Responsible Tech ecosystem — mapping organizations, mentoring talent, and connecting people who want technology aligned with the public interest.

name: Partnership on AI
description: A multistakeholder nonprofit uniting industry, civil society, and academia to develop shared norms for AI that benefits people and society.

name: Psychology of Technology Institute
description: A nonprofit network of hundreds of behavioral scientists — psychologists, sociologists, philosophers, and computer scientists — advancing the science of the human-technology relationship so AI can be designed for psychological health.

name: Common Sense Media
description: The leading kids-and-technology nonprofit, now rating AI products for youth safety and running a dedicated institute studying how AI affects children and families.

name: Data & Society
description: An independent research institute studying the social implications of data-centric technologies — grounding AI debates in how systems actually land in people’s lives.

name: AI Now Institute
description: Policy research on the concentration of power in the AI industry — and what accountability to the public would actually require.

name: Mozilla Foundation
description: The nonprofit behind Firefox, campaigning and grantmaking for trustworthy AI — and a member of the Humanity AI funding coalition.

name: Gloo · Flourishing AI
description: A technology platform whose Flourishing AI initiative benchmarks how well AI models’ answers actually help people flourish, using seven research-backed dimensions from flourishing science.

name: Gallup
description: The global analytics firm whose World Poll underpins much of the world’s wellbeing evidence — and the fieldwork engine of the Global Flourishing Study.

name: Positive AI Labs
description: A nonprofit developing open-source datasets and evaluations that guide frontier AI models toward human values and a pluralistic understanding of human flourishing.

name: Center for Open Science
description: Champions open, reproducible research — hosting the Global Flourishing Study’s open data so the science of flourishing is verifiable by anyone.

name: John Templeton Foundation
description: Major philanthropic funder of the science of human flourishing — including the Global Flourishing Study — supporting research on character, meaning, and spiritual life in a technological age.

name: Humanity AI Fund
description: A $500 million, five-year pooled fund from ten major foundations — including Ford, MacArthur, Mellon, Mozilla, Omidyar, Packard, and Kapor — investing in a people-centered future where AI strengthens communities and human creativity.

name: Human Change Foundation
description: Philanthropy founded by Margarita Louis-Dreyfus supporting pro-human technology — including the Pro-Human AI Declaration and research on how digital technology shapes children’s mental health and wellbeing.

name: Gates Foundation
description: The world’s largest private foundation, directing AI toward equity — funding AI scaling hubs and locally led evaluations of AI tools for health, agriculture, and education in low- and middle-income countries.

name: Workday Foundation
description: Workday’s corporate philanthropy, focused on human thriving through work — funding career pathways and workforce resilience as AI transforms the labor market.

name: Patrick J. McGovern Foundation
description: A philanthropy bridging AI and social purpose, committing $73.5 million toward "AI for Humanity" — advancing AI that expands human potential and civic wellbeing.

name: Hopelab
description: A social innovation lab and impact investor advancing technology for adolescent mental health and wellbeing — backing research and ventures at the intersection of AI and young people’s thriving.

name: OECD · AI Policy Observatory
description: The intergovernmental hub tracking national AI policies, paired with the OECD’s long-standing work measuring what matters for people’s wellbeing ("How’s Life?").

name: Ada Lovelace Institute
description: An independent institute making data and AI work for people and society — known for rigorous research on public attitudes, regulation, and the real-world impacts of AI systems.

name: Thrive Global
description: Arianna Huffington’s behavior-change company, extending into AI health coaching — and a vocal advocate for AI as a "GPS for the soul" at the AHA Symposium.

name: GatherVerse
description: A community organization convening global summits on emerging technology and humanity — including its AI for Human Flourishing summit series.

name: World Wellbeing Movement
description: A coalition of business and policy leaders — incubated at Oxford’s Wellbeing Research Centre — working to put wellbeing metrics at the heart of business and government decision-making.

name: Center for Digital Thriving · Harvard GSE
description: A research and innovation center at the Harvard Graduate School of Education studying how young people can thrive in a tech-filled world — including youth-centered research on how teens actually use and imagine AI.

name: Schmidt Sciences · AI2050
description: A $125 million philanthropic initiative co-chaired by Eric Schmidt and James Manyika, funding exceptional researchers working on the hard problems that must go right for society to benefit from AI.

name: Ford Foundation
description: One of the largest social-justice philanthropies, funding technology in the public interest — and a member of the Humanity AI coalition for people-centered AI.

name: MacArthur Foundation
description: Major philanthropy supporting a more just and verdant world — a driving member of the $500M Humanity AI coalition investing in a people-driven future for AI.

name: Omidyar Network
description: Pierre Omidyar’s philanthropic investment firm, funding responsible technology — from digital wellbeing to AI governance — and a Humanity AI coalition member.

name: Knight Foundation
description: Funds informed and engaged communities — including major university investments in research on technology, AI, and the future of democracy.

name: Wellcome Trust
description: One of the world’s largest health foundations, funding research on mental health and digital technology — including locally led evaluations of AI health tools with the Gates Foundation.

name: The Jed Foundation
description: A leading nonprofit protecting emotional health and preventing suicide among teens and young adults — increasingly focused on how AI and social platforms shape youth mental health.

name: 5Rights Foundation
description: Works to build the digital world children deserve — behind age-appropriate design codes worldwide and advocacy for children’s rights in AI systems.

name: Humane Intelligence
description: A tech nonprofit led by Rumman Chowdhury building public-interest evaluation of AI — red-teaming and algorithmic assessments in service of society.

name: Encode
description: A youth-led movement advocating for safe and accountable AI — organizing young people into the policy conversations that will define their future.

name: The Future Society
description: An independent nonprofit advancing the responsible governance of AI — operationalizing principles into institutions, law, and practice worldwide.

name: Aspen Institute · Aspen Digital
description: The Aspen Institute’s technology program, convening leaders across sectors so that AI and the information ecosystem serve a healthy, connected society.

name: Noēsis Collaborative
description: A nonprofit building a collaborative ecosystem of leaders who research, build, and govern technology that advances human flourishing — through invitation-only salons, the Noēsis Institute, and HumanConnections.AI.

name: Current AI
description: A public-interest AI partnership launched at the 2025 Paris AI Action Summit with an initial $400 million — from France, Germany, Ford, MacArthur, Google DeepMind, Salesforce and others — funding open, accountable AI that serves global equity.

name: Tech Justice Law Project
description: A legal advocacy organization holding technology companies accountable for AI and platform harms — litigating landmark cases on behalf of families harmed by AI companions.

name: Dubai Future Foundation
description: Dubai’s government foundation for imagining and prototyping the future — host of the Dubai Future Forum, one of the world’s largest gatherings of futurists, with growing programs on AI and human potential.

name: GovTech Singapore
description: Singapore’s government technology agency, building citizen-centered digital services and applying AI for public good across the Smart Nation initiative.

name: UNESCO
description: The UN agency behind the first global standard on AI ethics — the Recommendation on the Ethics of AI, adopted by 194 member states with human dignity and flourishing at its core.

name: European AI Office
description: The European Commission body implementing the EU AI Act — the world’s first comprehensive AI law — to ensure AI in Europe is trustworthy and human-centric.

name: MIT RAISE
description: MIT’s Responsible AI for Social Empowerment and Education initiative — headquartered at the MIT Media Lab and led by Cynthia Breazeal — advancing AI literacy so everyone can flourish in an AI-shaped world.

name: Artist and the Machine
description: A bi-annual convening of decision-makers at the intersection of creativity and AI — exploring how AI reshapes meaning, authorship, and human expression.

name: World Economic Forum · AI Governance Alliance
description: A multistakeholder alliance of industry, government, and civil society convened by the World Economic Forum to steer responsible AI development and inclusive access worldwide.

name: Doris Duke Foundation
description: A national foundation building a more creative, equitable and sustainable future through programs in the arts, child wellbeing, the environment, medical research and bridge-building — and a founding member of the $500M Humanity AI coalition.

name: Kapor Foundation
description: Works at the intersection of racial equity and technology to build a more equitable tech sector — expanding computing and AI education, funding responsible AI solutions, and advancing equitable technology policy. A founding member of the Humanity AI coalition.

name: Lumina Foundation
description: An education-focused foundation working to make learning beyond high school available to all, with a 2040 goal for credential attainment — and a founding member of the Humanity AI coalition, where it focuses on AI and the future of learning.

name: Mellon Foundation
description: The nation’s largest supporter of the arts and humanities, founded on the conviction that they are essential to human understanding — and a founding member of the Humanity AI coalition, where it focuses on creative work and artist ownership in the age of AI.

name: David and Lucile Packard Foundation
description: A family foundation working toward just and equitable communities, a healthy ocean and climate, and support for early-career scientists — and a founding member of the $500M Humanity AI coalition.

name: Siegel Family Endowment
description: A foundation whose mission is to understand and shape the impact of technology on society, funding inquiry-driven work across learning, work and infrastructure — including how workers get a voice in how AI reshapes employment. A founding member of the Humanity AI coalition.
